title: Data Centre Physical Layer: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A data centre is rows and rows of racks. Every one has to be cabled neatly. The physical layer matters more than you'd think.

scenes.heading: The utility grid
scenes.narration: Think of cables as a city's power and water. Copper runs stop at ninety metres, plus ten for patch cords. Fibre ignores electrical noise, and goes much further. Straight through cables need the same standard at both ends. And neat labelled racks make faults far easier to find.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Copper stops at a hundred metres. Fibre ignores interference. Use the same standard at both ends.

items.wrong: Different standards at each end are fine
